quotes.text: So here's the scandal. The bottleneck in business analytics isn't the data, it's the language.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the analytics bottleneck as a translation problem.

quotes.text: The brilliance of the design is that Copilot Studio inherits Fabric's governance instead of trying to reinvent it. You get convenience without chaos.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why natural-language access does not create a shadow security model.

quotes.text: AI removes gatekeeping but preserves governance. Copilot Studio doesn't hand everyone backstage passes to production databases.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the balance between democratization and control.

quotes.text: Preventing it isn't mystical. It's procedural, set clear system prompts instructing copilot to stay within fabric data, disable external web sources for critical data sets
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives concrete steps to reduce hallucinations in data agents.

chapters.title: Why this changes the analyst's job

takeaways: Copilot Studio translates natural-language questions into governed Microsoft Fabric queries through a published Fabric data agent, removing the SQL translation bottleneck.
Because queries run with the user's identity, Fabric's role-based access, row-level security and DLP still apply, and context trees let users refine follow-up questions.
Analysts shift from writing queries to curating semantics, prompts and guardrails, while organizations build data literacy and limit hallucinations with clear system prompts.
hook: Business users wait days for SQL reports while analysts translate questions into queries. This episode shows data and Power Platform teams how Copilot Studio and Fabric data agents let people ask questions in plain English while Fabric security stays in charge.
